title: Orchestrate Parallel Sectors -- Dated Incidents Ref
desc: T3 ref: dated incidents, calibration lessons, sortie proofs for the parallel-sector orchestration pattern.
steps: TIER RULE (2026-06-12): skill-ops sectors (authoring/enhancing skill content) go to a PRO-grade executor (Opus or Sonnet) or the orchestrator itself -- NEVER Haiku or Flash, which fabricate and drop skill content. See skill-contribute-edit and haiku-task-fabrication-detection.

FAMILY DIVERSIFICATION (user 2026-06-12): for parallel sectors, actively favor recently-strengthened OTHER-FAMILY executors (GPT/wkgpt, Gemini/wkgemini, Codex codex-mini/wkcodex, Groq, Cerebras, triad) on execution/analysis/refactor/error-fixing sectors -- pace-exempt, saves Claude budget. Keep skill-content authoring on Claude PRO.

EXPECTED-RESULT PRE-REGISTRATION (2026-06-22): while parallel delegations run, pre-write the EXPECTED RESULT for each dispatched agent BEFORE it returns. Return-time becomes a CHECK against the stated expectation -- any delta beyond expectation flags a silent drop, and you REVERT.

SORTIE PROOF (2026-06-23): in a 4-sector read-only sortie, the pre-registered-expected check caught 3 of 4 cheap specs wrong -- mis-attributed a signal, grepped the WRONG REPO, guessed the wrong layer. ALWAYS verify a cheap finding against source AND confirm WHICH REPO emits the symptom.
PUSH-WORKFLOW for a shared main that diverges: stash unstaged churn -> git pull --rebase origin main -> git push -> git stash pop.
